fields.summary: Add Integration test for rebuild from Fedora-generated OCFL

comments.body:
In initially setting up an environment for a "rebuild" integration test, I am running into the following functional errors:
...which seem very similar to those reported by Bethany Seeger:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1625#issuecomment-583113608

Steps to reproduce:

  1. Ensure Fedora is not running
  2. Clear persistence directories
    $ rm -rf /tmp/fcrepo.ocfl.*
  3. Start Fedora
    $ java -jar fcrepo-webapp/target/fcrepo-webapp-6.0.0-SNAPSHOT-jetty-console.jar --headless
  4. Create some resources
    $ curl -i -X PUT localhost:8080/rest/test
    $ curl -i -X PUT localhost:8080/rest/test/child
    $ curl -i -X PUT -H"Content-Type: image/jpeg" --data-binary @image.jpg localhost:8080/rest/binary
  5. Inspect newly created resources
    $ curl -i localhost:8080/rest/test
    $ curl -i localhost:8080/rest/test/child
    $ curl localhost:8080/rest/binary -o image-out.jpg
  6. Stop Fedora
  7. Start Fedora
  8. Inspect previously created resources
    $ curl -i localhost:8080/rest/test
    $ curl -i localhost:8080/rest/test/child
    $ curl localhost:8080/rest/binary -o image-out.jpg
  9. Stop Fedora
  10. Delete contents of the work dir
    $ rm -rf /tmp/fcrepo.ocfl.work.dir/*
  11. Start Fedora
    BOOM!
    Caused by: org.fcrepo.kernel.api.exception.RepositoryRuntimeException: Failed to rebuild fedora-to-ocfl index: Could not find .fcrepo/test_child.json within object test_child version null

The problem here is that the path to the sidecar file it's trying to load is computed differently on reload than when it's originally written.

AbstractRDFSourcePersister calculates that path from the id "test/child" to create the path "child.json", selecting the path part after the final slash character. However, on reload FedoraToOCFLObjectIndexUtilImpl maps the id "test_child" (which is the OCFL id of the same object) to "test_child.json". On reload, the subpath code does not generate the same path because the OCFL object id does not have a slash in it, because slashes in fedora ids are converted to underscores when they're turned into OCFL ids.
